* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Gila County in east central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 845 AM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of Pinto Creek and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations is occurring. Low-water crossings are
inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 453 AM MST, gauge reports on Pinto Creek indicated continued
flow. Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Roosevelt Estates.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 1 at 11:59PM EST until November 2 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
An upper level low will will continue to influence storms in the
Gulf and Bahamas through Monday. With the lack of a strong synoptic
surface forcing mechanism, predictability as to where and when heavy
rain will fall remains low. However, the environment continues to
support the potential for heavy rainfall and slow moving cells.

* WHAT...Heavy rain may cause, or worsen ongoing urban and street
flooding.

* WHERE...All of South Florida

* WHEN...Through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Isolated to scattered areas of flash flooding will be
possible, with the main impact being street flooding, road
closures, and limited impact to structures in flood prone areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Pockets of very heavy rainfall resulted in localized flash
flooding on Sunday and those areas, and others, have the
potential to be impacted again on Monday. Forecast amounts look
very similar to yesterday, with common amounts of 1 to 3 inches
where showers and storms occur. Scattered locations around south
Florida may see closer to 3 to 5 inches of rain. The more
isolated high end amounts have the potential to peak around 6 to
9 inches. These amounts could accumulate rather quickly, on the
order of 2 to 4 hours.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 7:26PM MST until November 2 at 7:30PM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
Upstream flooding along the Rio Grande continues downstream near
Monte Vista in Rio Grande County.

* WHAT...Flooding along the Rio Grande near Monte Vista is forecasted
to begin by late morning on Monday.

* WHERE...East Central Rio Grande County in south central Colorado...
West Central Alamosa County in southeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 730 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...The Rio Grande continues to rise due to upstream flooding
through Del Norte and South Fork. Extensive inundation of low-lying
areas adjacent to the river is expected. Inundation of low spots
along Highway 185, some homes, and other structures may be possible
for areas south of the river. Expect many areas of slow moving or
standing water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 717 PM MST, Upstream stream gauges on the Rio Grande and South
Fork Rio Grande indicate that flooding is occurring.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Monte Vista.
- http://water.noaa.gov
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
